runs.title: Ballon d'Or 2026: UK start time and how to watch
runs.prompt: Today is Sunday 26 October 2026. The 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony takes place in Paris this evening. Find out what time the ceremony starts in UK time, and how a viewer in the UK can watch it — which channel or streaming service is showing it, and whether it is free or paid.
runs.answer: The 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony starts at 8:00pm UK time (GMT) and runs until about 10:00pm, with red-carpet arrivals from 6:00pm (UEFA lists the ceremony as 20:00 GMT / 21:00 CET). UK viewers watch it free on DAZN — it holds the exclusive global rights and is streaming the show free of charge across ~200 markets; there is no paid subscription, you just need a free DAZN account (email sign-up) via the DAZN app or website (dazn.com/en-GB), and no UK terrestrial/linear channel is showing it. One correction to the brief: the ceremony is not in Paris this year — it's at the London Palladium (first time outside Paris for the 70th edition), and 26 October 2026 is a Monday, not a Sunday.

runs.title: Storm Boelo: power cuts and Met Office warnings
runs.prompt: Storm Boelo has battered parts of the UK over the last two days, causing deaths and widespread power cuts. It is now 26 October 2026. Find the current situation: how many properties are still without power, whether any Met Office weather warnings are still in force, and any official advice for people affected by the storm.
runs.answer: As of Monday afternoon 26 October 2026, the Energy Networks Association says about 22,600 properties are still without power after Storm Boelo — in Scotland, SSEN reports ~15,000 homes off supply in the north and SP Energy Networks ~500 in Ayrshire and Dumfries & Galloway, having restored nearly 100,000 over the weekend. Yes, Met Office warnings remain in force: a yellow wind warning from 18:00 Monday to 03:00 Tuesday for the west coasts of England, Wales and Scotland plus eastern Northern Ireland, and a second yellow wind warning for much of Scotland, parts of northern England and Northern Ireland from 03:00 Tuesday (BBC Scotland gives it ending 21:00, the national report 23:59). Official advice: the Met Office warns further power cuts are likely in warned areas and people should have essentials ready, including torches and batteries, expect travel delays and coastal spray/large waves; Sepa has an amber flood risk for the Northern and Western Isles and Caithness and Sutherland, and travellers should note school closures, ScotRail speed restrictions until 16:00 Tuesday, and CalMac/NorthLink ferry disruption.

runs.title: Packers officiating: what actually happened
runs.prompt: The Green Bay Packers lost their NFL Week 7 game and players publicly criticised the officials over roughing-the-passer penalties. Explain what actually happened: which penalties were disputed, what the players said, and whether the league or referees have responded. Prefer a source that loads without a paywall.
runs.answer: Green Bay lost 20-17 at Detroit on Oct. 25, 2026 (Week 7) on a late Lions field goal, and the postgame focus was officiating. The chief disputed roughing-the-passer flags were on Packers defenders Brenton Cox Jr. and Karl Brooks — the Brooks one coming with the score 17-17 and about 2:40 left, when an 18-yard completion to Sam LaPorta became a 15-yard penalty that extended Detroit's game-winning drive. Players were blunt: safety Xavier McKinney "unleashed" on the crew and said the refs have too much control, Devonte Wyatt (flagged for unnecessary roughness) also went after the officials, Keisean Nixon suggested the league has it in for Jordan Love, and Micah Parsons and even Tom Brady criticised the calls; Matt LaFleur mostly bit his tongue, saying no one heard a whistle on the Wyatt play and that Wyatt was playing to the whistle. The only official response was referee Alex Moore's postgame pool report, in which he defended the Wyatt unnecessary-roughness call and the intentional-grounding flag on Love — notably, he was not asked about the two roughing-the-passer penalties, and I found no NFL statement, admission of error or fine. Best paywall-free read: the Packers Wire pool-repor

runs.title: Mein Schiff 3 collision: damage and cruise line word
runs.prompt: The cruise ship Mein Schiff 3 was damaged in a collision with two container ships in Bremerhaven, Germany. What exactly happened, how severe is the damage, and what have the cruise line or port authorities said about the ship's next sailing?
runs.answer: Late on Sunday evening (25 October 2026), TUI Cruises' Mein Schiff 3 was departing Bremerhaven when a strong wind gust set her drifting and she struck two MSC container ships lying at the berths; the container ship suffered a large gash in its hull and several of Mein Schiff 3's lifeboats were torn apart/destroyed along her side, damage serious enough that the ship must go into a shipyard for repairs. TUI Cruises cancelled the ship's 20-night Canary Islands voyage that had just started, with passengers disembarking in Bremerhaven, and said affected guests would be informed about onward travel and later voyages as soon as the situation was reliably assessed. Bremerhaven water police are investigating the captain for a breach of duty of care, and the three vessels were reportedly barred from leaving port while the investigation continues.

runs.title: GPT-6.1 Terra: what it is and what it costs
runs.prompt: OpenAI has just announced a new model called GPT-6.1 Terra. Find out what it is, what its 'computer use' capability means for normal users, and how its price compares with the previous GPT-6.1 model.
runs.answer: GPT-6.1 Terra is OpenAI's new "fast and efficient" GPT-6.1-tier model in the API, sitting below GPT-6.1 Sol (balanced) and GPT-6 Astra (highest intelligence) and above GPT-6 Luna; it's aimed at visual reasoning, precise computer use and clean writing, with reasoning effort selectable from none to max (medium by default). Its computer-use capability means the model operates a browser or desktop itself — inspecting screenshots, clicking and typing to carry out multi-step tasks such as "acting on application screens," comparing drawings or matching product photos — rather than only replying in text; in the API this requires connecting it to a browser/desktop runtime. On price it is exactly half the previous GPT-6.1 model (Sol): $1.00 per 1M input and $5.00 per 1M output tokens vs Sol's $2.00/$10.00, $0.05 vs $0.10 cached input, and $2.00/$7.50 vs $4.00/$15.00 in long context.
